newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares in downtrend in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares in downtrend in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Eyyptian share prices slipped for the fifth day in a row on Thursday due to a long-running correction, the Capital Market Authority's report showed.
The CMA all-share index fell 0.31 points to 352.57 in trade worth 51.16 million pounds ($15 million).

"The correction has been going on for a long time and it forced people out of the market," said Ehab el-Mahallawi, account executive at Intercapital brokerage. "But I think people will come back once it's over."
Commercial International Bank/CIB was the most active on Thursday trading in 7.5 million pounds but it fell 0.75 pounds to close at 70.90.
"The price is excellent at this level and we may never see it again," said Mahallawi. "The low coupon forced people to sell."
CIB shares declined sharply after the bank announced a lower-than-expected dividend of two pounds per share for 1996.
The blue-chip cements disappeared from the list of most active shares due to shortage in supply, Mahallawi said.
"Cements were traded in high volumes at higher prices. But at these levels, shareholders keep their stock until prices go up again. There are no sellers but retail sellers now."
Recently privatised al-Ahram Beverages/ABC performed well, ending six pounds up at 130, after shares worth 7.3 million pounds were traded.
"News about an agreement with RC affected al-Ahram positively," Mahallawi said.
Al-Ahram said on Tuesday it had signed a letter of intent with Royal Crown (RC) Cola International to be exclusive producer of Royal Crown brands in Egypt.
The milling sector regained its active trade after investors realised that new wholly private sector millers would not affect the market share of the partially-privatised ones, Mahallawi said.
Many firms in the milling sector were once owned by the state, but shares were offered to the public as part of a privatisation-led reform programme.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills was the most active in the sector, but fell 0.50 pounds to close at 78.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 485.06 points from 485.42 points on Wednesday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms slipped to 260.15 from 260.4 points.
Out of the 92 shares traded, 34 rose, 42 fell while 16 ended unchanged.
